label: <DEL> step of long sequences that start with p (or k)
explanation: Fires almost only on the delimiter step (98% of mass; never in the copy phase; small activations on the last 1-2 original tokens before <DEL>), i.e. the step that outputs original token 0. The first original token is strongly selected: p (39x lift, 73% of mass) and secondarily k (12x, 18%). The rate also rises steeply with sequence length (none for L<=4, mostly L=8-9). Magnitude is largest for first token p, longer L, and specific second tokens (o, i, 2) and final tokens (f, e); top examples are all p-initial at L=7-9. The predicate (delimiter, first token p/k, L>=7) covers ~88% of activation mass but precision is only ~12%: most p/k-initial long sequences do not activate, and the additional dependence on orig(1) and the last input tokens is diffuse (adding them raises precision to ~38% but halves recall). Does not fire on other first tokens apart from a weak tail (o, t, r, 2).

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig0=p (+4.60), orig1=o (+3.60), orig2=o (+2.92), orig2=i (+2.80), orig1=i (+2.74), prev_tok=f (+2.65). Lower it: phase=2 (-4.45), orig5=- (-3.41), prev_tok=p (-2.35), prev_tok=k (-2.22).
